condition: VTE prophylaxis with high bleeding risk — day 1 after surgery for a bleeding duodenal ulcer
permutationLabel: High bleeding risk after surgery for bleeding DU
summary: 64-year-old man, day 1 after laparotomy and under-running of a bleeding duodenal ulcer, transfused, platelets 68: pharmacological prophylaxis should wait; mechanical prophylaxis now.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Ward review the day after emergency ulcer operation
inputs.hpi: Day 1 after laparotomy, duodenotomy and under-running of a bleeding posterior duodenal ulcer after failed endoscopic therapy. Received 6 units of red cells and 1 pool of platelets. One small melaena stool this morning. Haemoglobin stable overnight. Mobilising to the chair.

exam.general: Pale. HR 96, BP 118/70, RR 18, SpO2 97% on air, T 37.3°C.
exam.abdomen: Midline wound clean and dry, appropriately tender, soft. NG tube: bile only.

surgicalHistory: Laparotomy, duodenotomy and under-running of bleeding DU (day 1)

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Day 1 after under-running of bleeding duodenal ulcer — VTE prophylaxis decision (high bleeding risk)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Post-operative day 1, bleeding duodenal ulcer under-run, ongoing minor melaena, platelets 68. Bleeding risk currently outweighs VTE risk: mechanical prophylaxis now, reassess daily for LMWH.

mustInclude.note: Pharmacological prophylaxis contraindicated by active bleeding risk: mechanical prophylaxis, reassess daily.
mustInclude.proposedFix: See periop-vte-caprini-high-cancer-surgery; when bleeding risk outweighs VTE risk, suggest mechanical prophylaxis and a daily reassessment.

mustExclude.note: No unqualified LMWH on post-operative day 1 with ongoing melaena and platelets 68.

guideline.name: NICE NG89 — Venous thromboembolism in over 16s: reducing the risk of hospital-acquired DVT or PE
guideline.section: Assess VTE and bleeding risk; abdominal surgery with VTE risk above bleeding risk: pharmacological prophylaxis (LMWH) for at least 7 days; extended to 28 days after major cancer surgery in the abdomen/pelvis; mechanical prophylaxis (anti-embolism stockings or IPC) when pharmacological prophylaxis is contraindicated by bleeding risk; reassess within 24 h and when the clinical situation changes
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. VTE in over 16s (NG89). London: NICE; 2018 (updated 2019).

guideline.name: ACCP 9th edition — prevention of VTE in non-orthopaedic surgical patients (Caprini)
guideline.section: General and abdominal-pelvic surgery: Caprini ≥5 high risk → LMWH/LDUH plus mechanical prophylaxis; extended-duration (4 weeks) LMWH after abdominal/pelvic cancer surgery; high bleeding risk → mechanical prophylaxis until bleeding risk diminishes
guideline.citation: Gould MK, Garcia DA, Wren SM, et al. Chest. 2012;141(2 Suppl):e227S–77S.

rationale: Permutation: bleeding risk outweighs VTE risk. The index action is mechanical prophylaxis with daily reassessment, and no unqualified LMWH.
